data.gender_notes: Samidhaa is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The name Samidhaa is derived from Sanskrit and is the name of a goddess in Hindu mythology. She is the goddess of wealth, prosperity, and abundance. She is often depicted with a lotus flower in her hands and is believed to bring good fortune and riches to those who pray to her. The name Samidhaa carries the meaning “Goddess of Wealth” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Samidhaa usually hope their child will grow to embody goddess of wealth and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the abundant blessings of the divine goddess.
data.etymology: Samidhaa belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Goddess of Wealth.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Samidhaa total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

vedic_reference.note: Samidha is a Vedic goddess of sacrifices, fire, and fertility. She is often depicted as a wife of Agni, the god of fire, and is invoked in various rituals and sacrifices.

historical_references.reference: Samidhaa was the daughter of the Chera King, Senguttuvan. She played a significant role during the invasion of the Chola king Kulothunga Chola I in 1118 AD.

Samidhaa was a renowned poetess and a devotee of Lord Shiva, who lived during the Alvars period (8th-12th centuries AD). Her hymns are included in the Tirumurai, the twelve Tamil anthologies of the Shaiva Siddhanta tradition.
